em-16:
Dear Ms. Duarte,

I am a senior history major writing a thesis on how mapmakers portrayed the growth of our city's harbor between 1850 and 1920. Your collection of nineteenth-century port maps is the only one in the region that covers this period in detail, so examining the originals is essential to my research. Unfortunately, the digital copies do not show the handwritten notes in the margins, which are central to my argument.

My difficulty is one of timing. As part of my degree, I am completing a required internship at the Maritime Heritage Museum from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. every weekday this semester. Because special collections is open only on weekday mornings, I have not been able to visit at all.

Would it be possible to arrange supervised access on two afternoons per month? I would be happy to work during a staff member's regular hours, follow all handling rules, and request specific maps a week in advance so they could be prepared beforehand.

Thank you for considering this request.

Sincerely,
Isabel
em-17:
Dear Coach Abara,

Thank you for asking for our feedback on the new training schedule. I can already see some benefits: our fitness has clearly improved, and the extra sessions have given us more time to work on set pieces, which helped us beat Eastfield last week.

However, several teammates and I have some concerns. Because the morning sessions start at 6 a.m. three days a week, many of us are getting only five or six hours of sleep. We feel exhausted in afternoon classes, and a few players say their grades are slipping. More worrying, we've had four minor injuries in the past month, compared with one in the entire previous season, and I suspect fatigue is a factor.

I'd like to suggest reducing the early sessions to two days a week and making one of them a lighter recovery session focused on stretching and tactics. That way, we would keep most of the fitness gains while giving our bodies time to recover, which should mean fewer injuries and a stronger squad for the playoffs.

Respectfully,
Tyler
em-18:
Dear Dr. Feldman,

Thank you for organizing such a well-run conference last weekend. The keynote on coastal ecosystems was inspiring, the sessions ran on time, and the networking lunch gave me the chance to meet researchers I had only read about.

I would, however, like to comment on the poster session. The posters were placed in the narrow hallway behind registration, which most attendees passed only on their way to the restrooms. Because the session also overlapped with two popular talks, very few people came by. In ninety minutes, I spoke with only three visitors, and the presenter next to me had none at all.

For next year, I would suggest holding the poster session in a central space, such as the main lobby, at a time when no talks are scheduled. Serving coffee nearby would also encourage people to stay. Finally, a short preview session in which each presenter gives a one-minute summary would help attract an audience.

Best regards,
Min-jun
em-19:
Hi Priya,

I hope everything is okay with you. I noticed you weren't at our last two planning meetings, and since that's not like you at all, I wanted to check in. If something is going on, whether it's with classes, work, or something personal, I hope you know you can talk to me.

I also need to be honest about the project, though. With the presentation due on the 28th, we're at the point where everyone's sections need to come together. Without your part on the survey results, we can't finalize our conclusions, and a couple of people in the group are starting to feel stressed and a bit frustrated.

Could we meet for coffee this week, just the two of us, to figure out a plan? If your schedule is tight right now, we could adjust the workload, or I could take over part of your section while you focus on the data analysis. I just want to make sure we finish this together.

Take care,
Hannah
em-20:
Dear Professor Watanabe,

I hope your semester is going well. I am writing to follow up on the email I sent on September 12 asking whether I might join your lab as an undergraduate research assistant next semester. I understand that you receive many messages, so I wanted to make sure mine had not been overlooked.

The timing is somewhat urgent because the department's deadline for registering research credit is October 15, just ten days from now. If I am able to work in your lab, I would need your approval before then in order to fit it into my schedule.

To briefly restate my background, I am a third-year civil engineering student with a 3.8 GPA, and I earned an A in hydraulics. Last summer, I interned with the city's water department, where I helped map aging pipelines using GIS software. Your research on stormwater management in dense urban areas is exactly the field I hope to pursue in graduate school.

Thank you very much for your time.

Sincerely,
Arjun Mehta
em-21:
Dear Mr. Castillo,

I received your notice about the fifteen percent rent increase beginning next month, and I am writing to share a concern. According to Section 7 of our lease, any change to the rent requires at least sixty days' written notice. Since the notice was delivered on March 15, I believe the increase cannot take effect before mid-May.

Beyond the timing, an increase of this size would be very difficult for me. My rent would rise by $210 a month, which is more than my entire monthly grocery budget. I would have to move out, even though I would much prefer to stay.

Over the past two years, I have paid on time every month and taken good care of the unit. With that in mind, I would like to propose a compromise: an increase of eight percent starting in mid-May, in line with the required notice period, with a further review when the lease is renewed next year.

I hope we can find an arrangement that works for both of us.

Sincerely,
Grace Liu
em-22:
Dear Amira,

Thank you for telling me honestly how my comment at last week's practice tournament affected people. I owe you, and especially Daniel, an apology. When I called his argument "obviously naive" in front of the whole room, I was dismissive and disrespectful, and there is no excuse for that. I have also apologized to him personally.

Looking back, I realize I was so focused on winning the round that I forgot the purpose of a practice tournament. It is supposed to be a place where members, especially newer ones, can take risks and test ideas without fear of being mocked. A good debater challenges arguments, not people, and I failed to do that.

To help make the club more respectful, I would like to suggest that we agree on a short code of conduct at the next meeting, including a rule about criticizing ideas rather than individuals. I would also be glad to lead a brief workshop on giving constructive feedback, since I clearly need the practice myself.

Sincerely,
Owen
em-23:
Dear Ms. Lindqvist,

Thank you for asking us for ideas about attracting younger customers. I have one that I think could work well.

Over the past few months, I've noticed that the café next door is full of students every afternoon and evening, studying for hours. Many of them pass our window, but very few come inside, perhaps because they see bookstores as places to browse quickly rather than to spend time.

My proposal is a weekly "Study Night" every Wednesday from 6 to 9 p.m. We could set up a few tables in the back corner, offer free Wi-Fi, and give attendees ten percent off study guides and novels. Once a month, a local author could give a short talk.

The store would benefit by turning those café visitors into regular customers who discover our books while they are already here. The costs would be modest: a few folding tables, some posters for nearby campuses, and one extra staff member during those hours, a shift I would be happy to cover.

Best regards,
Lucas
em-24:
Dear Mr. and Mrs. Okonkwo,

Welcome to Linden Road! My name is Clara, and I live in the yellow house right next door. I hope the move went smoothly and that you're starting to feel settled. Please don't hesitate to knock if you ever need anything.

I'm also writing to tell you about our community garden day, which takes place every spring. This year, it will be held on Saturday, April 20, from 9 a.m. to noon in the small park at the end of the street. Neighbors work together to plant flowers, clean up the paths, and build new vegetable beds. Really, it's a chance to get to know one another, and we always finish with a potluck lunch.

You'd be very welcome to join us, even for just an hour. There are tasks for every age and energy level, from planting to painting signs with the children or simply bringing a dish to share. Of course, there's no obligation at all; I just wanted you to know you're invited.

Warm regards,
Clara
em-25:
Dear Customer Relations Department,

I am writing to request a refund and compensation for a canceled journey. On June 6, I held a ticket for the 7:15 a.m. train from Millbrook to Ashford (ticket number RX-40981). When I arrived at the station, the departure board simply showed "canceled," and no staff member could tell me when the next train would run or offer an alternative.

This cancellation had serious consequences for me. I was traveling to a job interview scheduled for 10 a.m. To get there, I had to buy a last-minute bus ticket for $68, more than twice the price of my train fare. Even so, I arrived forty minutes late, which made a poor first impression on the hiring committee.

I am therefore requesting a full refund of my $32 train ticket, as well as reimbursement for the $68 bus fare. Because the cancellation came with no notice and no assistance, I believe it is reasonable for the company to cover the costs it caused. I have attached copies of both tickets.

Sincerely,
Martin Kovač
em-26:
Dear Dr. Adeyemi,

I understand that you are reviewing student feedback on the recent change to the library's weekend hours, and I would like to share my experience. I am a part-time student in the business program, and I work full-time at a hospital from Monday to Friday. As a result, weekends are the only time I can study on campus.

Since the library began closing at 2 p.m. on Saturdays and staying closed on Sundays, I have lost almost all of my study time there. I do not have a reliable computer at home, so I now struggle to complete online assignments. Several classmates are in similar situations, including parents who can study only while their partners look after the children on weekends.

As an alternative, would the library consider closing earlier on one or two weekday evenings instead? The building is nearly empty after 8 p.m. on Fridays. Another option would be to keep one floor open on Sundays with minimal staff and self-checkout machines.

Thank you for considering students like me.

Respectfully,
Rosa Delgado
em-27:
Hi Marcus,

Now that orientation is over, I wanted to thank you for leading such an amazing team this year. You kept everyone organized without ever making the work feel stressful, and you always made sure that even first-year members like me had a voice in planning. The high ratings from new students show how much your leadership paid off.

Being on the committee taught me a lot. I learned how to plan events for over 800 people, how to adapt quickly when things go wrong, like the day the campus tour had to move indoors because of the storm, and how to speak confidently in front of large groups. It also gave me a much stronger sense of belonging at the university.

Since you're forming next year's committee, I'd love to be considered for the role of activities coordinator. I have some ideas for making the evening events more inclusive, such as adding quieter options for students who don't enjoy big parties. I'd also be glad to help train the new first-year representative.

Thanks again,
Jasmine
em-28:
Dear Sofia,

I'm so sorry, but I won't be able to come to your graduation party next Saturday. My company just told me that I must attend a mandatory two-day training session in Chicago starting that same morning. I asked my manager whether I could join a later session, but everyone in my department has to attend this one. I feel terrible about letting you down, especially after promising to give the speech.

Please know how much this celebration means to me. I've watched you work so hard for four years, through late nights in the library and that difficult final project, and I was really looking forward to telling everyone how proud I am of you.

I'd still love to be part of the day somehow. I could write the speech and record a video for your sister to play at the party. And when I get back, I'd like to take you out to dinner at that Italian place you love, just the two of us, to celebrate properly.

With love and congratulations,
Nina
em-29:
Dear Mr. Osei,

Thank you for considering me to lead the new Harper Foods project. I'm excited by the opportunity, both because I admire the client's brand and because leading a project of this size is exactly the kind of challenge I've been hoping for.

Before I accept, though, I want to be honest about my current workload. I'm responsible for the Lakeside Hotels campaign, which launches on the 18th, and the quarterly report for Vesta Insurance, due on the 30th. Both require a great deal of attention this month, and I'm concerned that taking on a third major project now could affect the quality of all three.

I'd like to propose a plan. Could Rachel, who has worked with me on the Vesta account, take over the final edits of that report? That would free up about ten hours a week. I could also lead the initial client meeting next week but begin the main work on the 19th, after the hotel campaign launches. That way, I could give the new project my full attention.

Best regards,
Elise
em-30:
Dear Dr. Marchetti,

Thank you very much for accepting my paper, "Low-Cost Salt Batteries for Residential Solar Storage," for an oral presentation. It is an honor to be included in the program, and I am looking forward to sharing my results.

Unfortunately, I have a scheduling problem. My talk is listed for 9:30 a.m. on the first day of the conference, but I have a required final exam at my university the day before, and it cannot be moved. The earliest flight I can take lands at 1 p.m. on the first day, so I would not arrive in time.

I can think of a few possible solutions. Ideally, I could present at any time on the second or third day. If that is not possible, I would be glad to exchange slots with another presenter, or, as a last resort, give my talk remotely by video. I would prefer the first option, since presenting in person would allow me to discuss my work with other researchers more fully.

Thank you for your understanding.

Best regards,
Amara Singh
